episodes.title: Could Huang Return,  AI Trade Turmoil and New China Chip Rules
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
A sharp AI-trade sell-off (Nasdaq 100 -2.5%, S&P -1.5%, Nvidia -4-4.5%) coincides with Commerce Department chip export rules closing a China loophole, landing on the eve of Trump's Beijing-area summit with Xi and Putin. JPMorgan's David Kelly also makes a contrarian dovish Fed call, with implications for USD, UST yields and broad risk appetite that matter to EM carry trades.

**Key points**
- Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's board is not considering reinstating him despite a petition signed by hundreds of thousands (incl. Elon Musk); investigation led by Wachtell Lipton's June Kim, no timeline, no search firm hired yet.
- Broad AI/semis/data-center complex down 6-7% (ARM, SanDisk, Dell); Nvidia testing last week's 148 intraday low.
- Commerce closed an export-control loophole letting Chinese firms rent AI compute via third countries (Malaysia, Singapore); rule explicitly drafted "at the direction of" Treasury/NSC, reportedly overriding a reluctant Commerce Secretary Lutnik.
- 10-year UST yield eased to ~5.12-5.14%.
- David Kelly (JPM): expects only one more Fed hike, citing soft vehicle sales, weak housing, no wage inflation, 10y breakeven at 2.22%, and falling Nov oil/gas prices (~0.3ppt off YoY CPI) — sees inflation past its second 2026 peak.
- Anthropic IPO set for Thursday at ~$1.4tn valuation; narrative of capital rotating from AI infrastructure to AI application layer.
- JPMorgan Chase/other major US banks (BofA, Wells Fargo, US Bank) and Zelle hit by a technical outage, described as a bug not a cyberattack.

**FX / rates implications**
- A less-hawkish Fed path (Kelly's one-hike call, falling oil feeding into CPI) would be USD-negative and supportive of EM carry (INR, IDR, PHP, MXN, BRL) if consensus shifts; watch this week's Fed speakers for confirmation.
- Sustained US equity/AI-trade risk-off is a classic EM headwind, pressuring high-beta EM FX and widening credit spreads if it persists beyond a single-sector unwind.
- Escalating US-China tech/export friction right before the Trump-Xi meeting raises retaliation risk via China's rare-earths lever, a tail risk for CNY/CNH and broader EM Asia FX sentiment.
- Sharply lower oil/gas prices are disinflationary and currency-supportive for EM oil importers (India, Philippines, Thailand) but a drag for oil-linked LATAM credits (Mexico, Colombia).

**Watch list**
- Nvidia earnings call (day after this taping) for China/export exposure and CEO-succession updates.
- Anthropic's Thursday IPO as a gauge of AI-trade risk appetite.
- Trump's China trip and any rare-earths retaliation signal.
- This week's heavy Fed-speaker slate for pushback on, or confirmation of, Kelly's dovish one-hike view.
